findings.source: Diamond.FacetCut[] memory emptyFacetCuts = new Diamond.FacetCut[](0); ... emit NewUpgradeCutData(_newProtocolVersion, _cutData);
findings.issue: The ABI-encoding loop over the empty facetCuts array has its exit test folded to true, but the loop is kept: 'while True' starts with the log and 'stop', followed by a dead body with its own nested while. The same encoding for the first NewUpgradeCutData event (line 781) is folded completely, so the function shows a loop that never runs.
findings.rule: When a loop's exit test is constant true on entry (index 0 against a known length 0), replace the loop by its exit path and drop the body.

findings.issue: Errors written at the free pointer are left as raw reverts, even 'revert with memory from mem[64] len 4' right after storing the ZeroAddress selector at mem[mem[64]], while createNewVerifierOnlyUpgrade shows the same three errors decoded (lines 741, 743, 783). The migrationPaused() static call, executeUpgrade, upgradeChainFromVersion and genesisUpgrade calls keep raw argument memory, and the lengths contain '_15 + ceil32(return_data.size) - mem[64]' terms that are constants.
findings.rule: Decode a revert or call whose data start is symbolic when the word at that start holds a known selector; treat a variable assigned mem[64] as equal to mem[64] until the next store to slot 64 so these lengths fold.
findings.verified: by reading: _15 = mem[64] and mem[64] = ceil32(return_data.size) + mem[64] on lines 1077-1078, so the error store at mem[_15 + ceil32(return_data.size)] is at the new mem[64]

notes: No explicit loops in EraChainTypeManager/ChainTypeManagerBase or the libraries they reach (source_loops 0). All 37 text whiles are implicit: decoding/encoding of DiamondCutData (FacetCut[] with nested bytes4[] selectors), calldata copies and event encodings (P7); the zero-trip one in createNewVerifierOnlyUpgrade is reported. isZKsyncOS's 'const = 0' is the real 'return false'. Version checks, SemVer unpacking, deadlines, cut-hash bookkeeping, StoredBatchInfo hashing, the CREATE2 deployment and the order of checks in createNewChain all match the source; reentrancyGuardInitializer's store before its check is harmless (revert undoes it).
summary: All 60 functions reviewed; the text is semantically faithful (immutables aside) and has no source loops. Problems: a zero-trip encoding loop kept as 'while True' with stop first and a dead body, and errors and calls written at the free pointer left as raw memory in setNewVersionUpgrade, createNewChain and the upgrade forwarders while the same errors are decoded elsewhere.
